title: Arkret Account Data Self-Management Operation DTOs
description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface actor-private account_data operations (ak.self.account_data.*). PUT builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write; the server stores content verbatim (clients own canonical encoding and, for sensitive keys, client-side encryption). Every key is a server-versioned compare-and-set whole-value register: writes carry expected_revision and the accepted revision is expected_revision + 1, so concurrent multi-device writes converge instead of silently overwriting each other. See spec/v1/zh/models/account-data.md §5. account_data_key keys are dot-delimited namespaces validated against account-data-key-registry.json.

account_data_key.description: Dot-delimited account_data namespace key (e.g. ak.contacts.realm.<realm_id>, ak.account.blocklist). Control chars / whitespace / path separators are forbidden so the key is URL- and log-safe.

revision.description: Monotonic per-key revision counter. 0 means the key has never been written. Each accepted write or delete stores expected_revision + 1. The counter is a high-water mark: it MUST NOT go backwards, not even after a tombstone is garbage-collected, so a stale offline write can never resurrect a superseded value.
Revision of this stored value. Pass it back as expected_revision to replace or delete the entry.

content.description: Caller-supplied opaque payload, stored verbatim. Any JSON value.

expected_revision.description: Compare-and-set precondition: the revision the caller believes is current. Use 0 to create a key that has never been written. A mismatch MUST fail with cas_conflict and MUST NOT store the value.

content.description: Caller-supplied opaque payload. Server stores it verbatim; canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption are the client's responsibility. Any JSON value.

revision.description: Revision of the stored tombstone (expected_revision + 1). Recreating the key requires this value as the next expected_revision.

account_data_cas_conflict_details.description: Closed error.details payload for cas_conflict and not_found on ak.self.account_data.resource.*. It always carries the current revision so the caller can decrypt, re-apply its domain merge rule and issue exactly one new compare-and-set write without a second round trip.

current_entry.description: Present only when the key currently holds a live value. Omitted when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; current_revision is still authoritative in that case.
